messages:
lina: quick design check — thinking about a 'fail-open hedging' mode for ingress when we detect sustained backpressure. proposal: short hedges (50-200ms) to a low-cost fallback pool + requeue the original into a low-priority admission queue instead of immediate 503s. want to avoid thundering retries and keep tail latency bounded. :thinking:

tim: can you expand on 'low-priority admission queue'? how do we prevent starvation from bursty clients?

lina: good q. idea is to have two requeue buckets: low-pri (longer wait, can be preempted) and deferred (for best-effort retries). admission policy uses token-bucket per-tenant + a max-latency watermark so we don't keep requests indefinitely.

ajay: i'm worried about side effects + exactly-once behavior. hedging can cause duplicate ops. we need opt-in headers or idempotency keys at the gateway. otherwise we risk double writes.

lina: agreed. hedging only enabled for idempotent routes or when X-Idempotency-Key present. non-idempotent => fast-fail 503 or queue to a human ops flow.

diego: telemetry question — how do we surface cost impact? hedging increases downstream qps. we should tag hedged requests in traces and metrics: span tag hedged=true and metric ingress.hedges.count. also record which fallback pool served it.

olivia: +1 for trace tags. also add a sampling rule so we don't blow up traces during big floods. maybe 5% of hedged flows get full trace.

lina: agreed on sampling. another thing: hedging timebox should be adaptive. baseline = 100ms but backoff if fallback is already saturated. If fallback latency climbs, reduce hedging rate via simple AIMD.

tim: Implementation nit: do we hedge on the same connection or open new upstream conns? Opening new conns is heavier. Could we use a shared connection pool and tag the request as hedged so upstream can treat it accordingly?

ajay: upstreams might not be able to treat hedged requests specially. safer to route to a different pool (fallback variant) that has separate autoscaling. avoids cascading overload.

lina: yep — plan is: primary pool (normal), fallback pool (small, cheaper instances, maybe quantized model variants). routing rule: if ingress detects queueing > threshold -> spawn hedged request to fallback pool. primary still processes the original; when either responds first we cancel the other.

diego: cancel semantics important. need reliable cancel propagation to upstream or we'll leak work. propose adding an ingress-cancel token header our runtime understands and cancels KV-cache/execution. upstream adaptors must implement cancel hook.

olivia: and billing — we need to surface hedged token cost back to customers. otherwise teams see token spikes. maybe mark tokens as hedged_cost and expose in per-route console.

lina: yep — billing plan: record tokens from hedged responses separately, include in logs + console. default: charge hedged at 50%? open for debate.

tim: small config example for ops/devs so this is concrete:

```yaml
ingress:  # per-route
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    max_inflight_hedges: 2
    timebox_ms: 100
    fallback_pool: lowcost-v1
    idempotent_only: true
    sampling_rate: 0.05
```

ajay: +1 on config. we should also expose runtime flags to force fail-open vs fail-closed for debugging.

diego: edge-case: if primary responds with partial stream and fallback returns full — which do we prefer? prefer whatever completes more tokens; but need deterministic tie-break: prefer primary unless fallback is ahead by >N tokens to avoid jitter.

lina: good point. tie-break rule: prefer first response completion signal; for streaming, prefer whichever has emitted >alpha tokens beyond the other in a 2s window. alpha = 16 default.

olivia: can we add a canary gate? enable hedging for 5% of traffic first, then ramp based on latency and cost metrics.

lina: yes — rollout plan: 5% canary (non-critical routes) -> monitor p99, hedged_cost, error rate -> 25% -> full. I'll put a dashboard query: ingress.hedges.count, ingress.hedges.p99_latency, ingress.hedges.extra_cost_tokens.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure fallback pool autoscale limits set, add cancel-hook tests, add throttles on hedged QPS, add billing tag pipeline.

tim: next actions: lina to write short RFC stub with config, metrics, and cancel semantics. ajay to spec idempotency header and migrate a couple of noncritical routes for canary. diego to add metrics instrumentation. olivia to create dashboard. I'll volunteer to review.

lina: thanks — i'll draft RFC today and ping this thread when ready. :slightly_smiling_face:
